A 24-day march led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, from his ashram near Ahmedabad to the sea at Dandi, about 390 kilometres away, to break the British salt law.

Britain taxed salt and kept a monopoly on making it, which hit the poorest hardest. Gandhi chose it because everyone used salt. He set off on 12 March with 78 followers, and thousands joined along the way, with reporters and film crews watching. At Dandi on 6 April he picked up a lump of natural salt from the mud, an illegal act.

People across India began making salt and boycotting British goods, which started the civil disobedience movement. Around 60,000 were jailed, Gandhi among them in May. In late May Sarojini Naidu led about 2,500 volunteers at the Dharasana salt works, where police beat them. Reports from American journalist Webb Miller carried the scene to the world.

Gandhi was released and signed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931. The march made the Raj look cruel, and made Gandhi's nonviolence a model for later movements.
sum: A 24-day march led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, from his ashram near Ahmedabad to the sea at Dandi, about 390 kilometres away, to break the British salt law.
